## What this is

`skill_management` puts a control panel on the skills installed in your OpenCode setup. It can list them, explain why one is unavailable, hide one from the model, and bring it back.

Disabling never touches skill files: it writes a single `skill` permission rule into your global config (`effect: "deny"`, or `"ask"` for a soft disable). Nothing is deleted, moved or rewritten, and removing the rule restores the skill exactly as it was.

| Action | What it does | Writes config |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | Every registered skill with its effective state for the calling agent (`available` / `disabled` / `ask`) | no |
| `inspect` | Why one skill is (un)available: the matching rule, per-agent differences, how its id was derived | no |
| `disable` | Hide it from the model and reject loading it (`effect: "ask"` keeps it listed and asks on load) | yes |
| `enable` | Remove the blocking rule again, whoever wrote it | yes |

Install in one command: `opencode plugin add github:sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management` (details below).

## What's changed since v0.1.0

**Fixed — `list` reported the wrong state.** It merged every agent's permission rules before evaluating them, so deny rules owned by sub-agents (`explorer`, `title`, …) leaked into the caller's result: on a stock setup 28 of 29 skills showed up as `disabled` while `inspect` said they were available. States are now evaluated against the calling agent only — the output names that agent, and adds a one-line hint when other agents disagree (which is normal for sub-agents that deny everything).

**Added — one-command verification on Linux / WSL.** `tools/linux-verify.sh` puts Node and the OpenCode CLI in a temporary directory under `$HOME`, runs the full acceptance suite (175 assertions), confirms a real OpenCode host loads the plugin, then cleans up after itself. No `sudo`, no writes to your real config.

**Docs — README rewritten for users.** It now leads with the problem the tool solves and explains the four actions (`list` / `inspect` / `disable` / `enable`): what each one does, when to reach for it, and whether it writes configuration.

**Verified.** 175 assertions pass on Windows and on Linux (Debian 13.5, OpenCode 2.0.32). The `disable → rejected load → enable` round trip was re-run on a Linux host: the skill disappears from the model-visible list, loading it is rejected, and `enable` restores it.

## Install or upgrade

```pwsh
# via git (no registry, no token)
opencode plugin add github:sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management

# via npm
opencode plugin add opencode-skill-management@0.2.0
```

**Offline / single file:** download `skill_management.js` from the assets below and drop it into `<config>/plugins/`. The `opencode-skill-management-0.2.0.tgz` asset is the exact npm tarball if you prefer to unpack it yourself.

Confirm it is loaded:

```pwsh
opencode plugin list --builtin
# skill_management   local   <config>/plugins/skill_management.js
```

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management/compare/v0.1.0...v0.2.0
